note: The modern RV toilet water valve families, and what each one fits. Every entry is recorded against a maker document named in sources, and each of those documents was fetched and read on 2026-10-10 rather than taken from a parts retailer's compiled list. Where a number could not be confirmed against a maker document, the family is still covered, the number is recorded here with source_status owed, and the page does not print it. The structure follows the competitor's model, which is its one good idea; the data is not theirs.

families.label: Dometic 300, 310, 320 and 400 series gravity toilets
families.valve_place: on the base, above the model label
families.bowl: Polypropylene on the 300 and 301, vitreous ceramic on the 310, 311, 320 and 321
families.seat: Polypropylene on the 300, 301, 310 and 311, enameled wood on the 320 and 321
families.source_note: Dometic's 310 manual names 385311641 as the water valve kit for the 310, and the 400 series page lists the same kit as its spare valve.

families.label: Dometic Traveler, Traveler Lite, EcoVac and VacuFlush toilets
families.flush: foot pedal, with a vacuum pump on the VacuFlush models
families.bowl: Deep bowl, with an elongated enameled wood seat on the 510HPS
families.source_note: The number 385314349 appears in retailer fitment lists and in Dometic's Sanitation Replacement Parts Guide, which Dometic serves as a download from its parts pages. No copy of that guide naming the number was fetched from a Dometic host, so the number is recorded here and is not printed on the tool page. Dometic's own manual for this family lists the water valve as a spare part held in the foot pedal, and names freeze damage and a leaking valve body as the reasons to replace it.

families.label: Thetford Aqua-Magic V and VI
families.flush: hand lever on the V, foot pedal on the VI
families.source_note: Thetford's install sheet for the water module kit covers the Aqua-Magic V and VI, and lists what the kit contains.

families.label: Thetford Aqua-Magic Residence and Style II
families.valve_place: under the pedal, with the pedal pulled off
families.bowl: Polypropylene on the Residence, ceramic on a polypropylene base on the Style II
families.source_note: Thetford's install sheet for the valve kit covers the Residence and the Style II, and shows the pedal coming off before the valve does.

on the back of the toilet, and on some models on the base

maker_questions.note: Thetford's own identification flow, printed here because it is the maker's method rather than ours. The tool asks the same kind of question.
questions: Is the unit a hand flush, foot flush, or wall panel flush?
If a hand flush: is it a mechanical lever or an electric button? If it is an electric button, does it have one button or two?
If a foot flush: does it have one or two pedals? Locate the pedals when sitting on the toilet, on the left side or the center.
If a wall panel flush: does it have one or two buttons or switches?
Is the bowl porcelain or plastic?

published_figures.note: Figures the makers publish for their own models. A tape measure settles the first two questions a person can answer at home.

bowl_material.material: Ceramic bowl on a polypropylene base

waste_gate.part_name: Blade seal, on a blade that slides
